rows.source: UKHSA West Nile virus surveillance and contingency planning
rows.verified: West Nile virus is a mosquito-borne infection maintained primarily in a bird-mosquito transmission cycle.

rows.source: UKHSA West Nile virus surveillance and contingency planning
rows.verified: UKHSA guidance covers epidemiology, diagnosis and prevention of West Nile virus.

rows.source: UKHSA West Nile virus surveillance and contingency planning
rows.verified: Specialist UKHSA testing can include antibody testing and PCR where clinically indicated.

rows.source: UKHSA West Nile virus surveillance and contingency planning
rows.verified: England has a national contingency plan for preparedness and response to West Nile virus.

rows.source: UKHSA West Nile virus surveillance and contingency planning
rows.verified: The contingency plan uses risk levels to guide public-health and local-authority actions.

rows.source: UKHSA West Nile virus surveillance and contingency planning
rows.verified: UKHSA can notify local authorities and health-protection teams when an area moves to a higher risk level during the transmission season.

rows.source: UKHSA West Nile virus surveillance and contingency planning
rows.verified: UK surveillance includes mosquitoes, birds, animals and human illness within a One Health approach.

rows.source: UKHSA West Nile virus surveillance and contingency planning
rows.verified: Detection of viral genetic material in mosquitoes does not by itself demonstrate established human transmission.

rows.source: UKHSA West Nile virus surveillance and contingency planning
rows.verified: West Nile risk depends on mosquito species and abundance, bird infection, season, weather, local surveillance, bite exposure and host factors.

rows.source: UKHSA West Nile virus surveillance and contingency planning
rows.verified: UKHSA West Nile evidence is vector-, animal-, location-, person-, surveillance- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: UKHSA yellow-fever vaccination and travel guidance
rows.verified: Yellow fever is a mosquito-borne viral infection relevant to travel in affected areas.

rows.source: UKHSA yellow-fever vaccination and travel guidance
rows.verified: UKHSA publishes yellow-fever guidance, data and analysis for health professionals and travellers.

rows.source: UKHSA yellow-fever vaccination and travel guidance
rows.verified: The Green Book provides national guidance on yellow-fever vaccination.

rows.source: UKHSA yellow-fever vaccination and travel guidance
rows.verified: Vaccination decisions require an individual risk-benefit assessment.

rows.source: UKHSA yellow-fever vaccination and travel guidance
rows.verified: Contraindications and precautions are especially important for people with weakened immunity.

rows.source: UKHSA yellow-fever vaccination and travel guidance
rows.verified: Strengthened precautions apply to people aged 60 years or older.

rows.source: UKHSA yellow-fever vaccination and travel guidance
rows.verified: International travel requirements may include proof of yellow-fever vaccination even where infection risk differs.

rows.source: UKHSA yellow-fever vaccination and travel guidance
rows.verified: Mosquito-bite prevention remains important alongside vaccination where yellow-fever exposure is possible.

rows.source: UKHSA yellow-fever vaccination and travel guidance
rows.verified: Yellow-fever risk and vaccine suitability depend on destination, itinerary, outbreak status, age, immune status, medical history and entry requirements.

rows.source: UKHSA yellow-fever vaccination and travel guidance
rows.verified: UKHSA yellow-fever evidence is destination-, traveller-, vaccine-, health-, requirement- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
